sources.entry: Mimer - Fast, private, developer-first clipboard manager with type-aware history, ⌘K transforms, and history encrypted at rest.

summary.one_liner: Mimer is a free, open-source, privacy-focused clipboard manager for macOS 14+ that keeps searchable, type-aware clipboard history and offers ⌘K text transforms.
summary.what_it_does: Mimer runs in the macOS menu bar and records copied items into a local Core Data history that persists across restarts. A palette opened with ⇧⌘V supports fuzzy search with scoped filters (type:, app:, is:fav, /regex/), and clips are auto-classified by type (links, code, colors, git SHAs, issue keys, file paths). The ⌘K transform engine reshapes a clip with a live preview, covering case changes, slugify, Base64/URL, JSON pretty-print and minify, JSON to TypeScript, JWT decoding, Unix/ISO time conversion, and more. Clip contents and source-app names are encrypted at rest with an AES-GCM key held in the Keychain, and detected secrets are masked on screen. The README also describes a paste-stack, favorites, snippets, per-app exclusions, importing history from Maccy, and a `mimer` CLI and `mimer-mcp` MCP server that expose the transform engine and, optionally, clip history to local AI tools.
use_cases: reformat or convert copied text (JSON, Base64, JWT, timestamps)
keep copied passwords and API keys hidden during screenshares
paste several copied items in sequence
use clipboard transforms from the terminal or scripts
let a local AI assistant access clipboard history
how_to_run: open Mimer.xcodeproj  (or: xcodebuild -scheme Mimer -configuration Release build)
notable: Type-aware clips with live color swatches and a hover preview that formats JSON, diffs, and URLs
Encrypted at rest (AES-GCM, Keychain key) with secrets masked on screen but still pasteable
Ships a mimer CLI and mimer-mcp server sharing the same ⌘K transform code as the app
Paste-stack queues several clips and pastes them in order
Imports history from Maccy, keeping original times, source apps, and pinned items
caveats: AI/MCP clip-reading access is off by default, and the local channel is unauthenticated while enabled
Encryption is at-rest only; losing the Keychain key makes stored history unreadable
Planned but not yet built: file clips, more transforms, OCR on images
